summary: In 1984 a methyl isocyanate leak at Union Carbide's cost-cut, badly maintained pesticide plant in Bhopal, India killed thousands overnight; the company dodged blame, paid a small settlement and left poison that still sickens residents.

evidence.note: 1976 union complaints open the cost-cutting and safety-decay narrative
worker deaths, injuries and repeated gas leaks in the early 1980s
unions campaign, hunger strike, leaders laid off and meetings banned
refrigeration shut-off approved with US headquarters; West Virginia sister plant contrast
gas release in the early hours of 3 December 1984
accounts of families and infants dying; autopsies of gas-filled lungs
1985 Gas Leak Disaster Act and later settlement with the Indian government
abandoned waste, leaking ponds and groundwater contamination
2018 reporting on birth defects and cancer in neighbourhoods by the plant
Dow, Eveready and the state trade blame for cleanup up to the release date

notes: Primary is the event; Union Carbide is secondary as the responsible company, so roles are empty. Main span ends at the 1989 settlement (year from general knowledge; the transcript gives the settlement without a date). Scope set international because US headquarters decisions and US lawsuits get real time, though the harm is in one city.
